overview: This bill directs the U.S. Forest Service, part of the Agriculture Department, to work with ranchers who hold federal grazing permits on a strategy to use livestock grazing to reduce wildfire risk. Grazing animals can eat down grasses and brush that would otherwise fuel fires. The strategy would include completing environmental reviews so ranchers can use empty grazing areas when drought, wildfire or other disasters disrupt their usual ones, more use of targeted grazing and temporary permits to cut down fire fuels and invasive grasses, and using grazing to help land recover after fires. As of January 8, 2026, the House Natural Resources Committee had approved an amended version.
for: Supporters say grazing is a low-cost, practical way to reduce dry vegetation that feeds wildfires, and the bill gives ranchers more flexibility when disasters strike.
against: Critics say expanding grazing on public lands can damage soils, streams and native plants if not carefully managed, and that speeding up approvals could shortchange environmental reviews.
